title: Director, Vanta for Government Partnerships
description:
At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. 



Vanta's V4G Partnerships function sits at the intersection of our platform, the government agencies and contractors we serve, and the broad network of systems integrators, resellers, service providers, and auditors within the public sector compliance and risk management ecosystem. You'll help build and grow these partnerships to build pipeline, as well as to ensure that customers have access to high-quality, trusted delivery through Vanta.

As Director, Vanta for Government (V4G) Partnerships, you will own Vanta's partner function for the public sector — the strategy, the network, and the programs that let it scale — supporting both our government sales motion (Federal and SLED) and our government vendor business. Reporting directly to the Head of Public Sector, you will define the partner archetypes, tiering, and coverage model required to serve government demand, and own V4G partner-sourced pipeline and ARR that rolls into Vanta's overall partner-sourced target. You'll work in close partnership with the VP of Global Channel & Alliances, who owns that overall target and channel operating model, to ensure the public sector motion is built on — and strengthens — that foundation. This is a high-impact, cross-functional role for someone who has built a public sector partner function from the ground up: designing joint GTM programs, negotiating enterprise partnership agreements, and standing up the mechanisms that let a partner network scale beyond the person running it.



You'll have meaningful scope: you'll own the V4G partner function — the strategy, the partner network, the program design, and the team — and decide how Vanta invests across public sector partners, including tiering, enablement investment, and where to expand or exit. You'll own the V4G partner-sourced pipeline and ARR contribution, and the coverage standard that determines how partner resources are leveraged and applied across Vanta’s government and commercial opportunities.You http://opportunities.You'll start with one partnerships manager and build the team as the segment grows, taking a “player-coach” approach to help establish that growth.



What you’ll do as a Director, Vanta for Government Partnerships at Vanta:

 - Own the V4G partner strategy across Federal and SLED — define the partner archetypes Vanta needs (resellers, service partners, GSIs, 3PAOs and C3PAOs), the tiering and coverage model, and the multi-year plan to build a network that meets government and commercial demand.

 - Own the V4G partner-sourced pipeline and ARR contribution to Vanta's partner-sourced target, and define the metrics by which public sector partner performance, partner health, and network coverage are measured — including the coverage standard for FedRAMP and CMMC delivery capacity.

 - Design the programs and mechanisms that let the network scale — partner tiering and certification, enablement paths, co-sell motion, MDF and investment allocation, partner health frameworks, and standardized partner agreements built with Legal.

 - Build and lead the V4G partnerships team, starting with one manager and scaling with the segment. Set the operating rhythms, quality bar, and performance standards, and develop the team to own partner relationships directly.

 - Partner with the VP of Global Channel & Alliances and the broader channel organization to extend the V4G motion across Vanta's full partner ecosystem — including MSPs, VARs, and auditors working on federal compliance programs like FedRAMP and CMMC — ensuring the public sector motion strengthens rather than duplicates the commercial one.

 - Serve as the voice of the government ecosystem inside Vanta, with a influence in V4G product roadmap, packaging, and pricing decisions — translating what partners, commercial customers, and government agencies need into a prioritized point of view Product and Engineering can act on.

 - Expand the network and reduce concentration risk by identifying and onboarding new firms, capturing demand from large partners not yet engaged, and making clear calls about where Vanta invests and where it walks away.



How to be successful in this role:

 - 10+ years of experience managing public sector channel and/or partnerships, with a strong network across GSIs, managed service providers, resellers, and auditors.

 - Deep familiarity with the public sector ecosystem, including Federal and SLED go-to-market motions and federal compliance programs, such as FedRAMP and CMMC.

 - 5+ years of people management experience, including managing performance across a team.

 - Experience owning a revenue target delivered through partners, including defining the metrics and operating cadence required to hit it.

 - Proven ability to build, manage, and grow external partner relationships at scale — ideally within cybersecurity, GRC, or compliance-adjacent ecosystems.

 - Experience partnering with systems integrators, MSPs, VARs, and audit firms; direct audit or assessor experience is a plus but not required.

 - Strong instincts for balancing technical/domain credibility with business development thinking

 - Track record of building or scaling a partner or channel network, reducing risk through diversification, or driving quality programs in an external-facing capacity

 - Demonstrated ability to coordinate cross-functionally across GTM, product, legal, marketing, and channel sales teams

 - Comfort navigating ambiguity and building structure in a fast-moving, high-growth environment

 - Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.

 - Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.



What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

 - Industry-competitive salary and equity

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans

 - 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents

 - Health & wellness stipend

 - Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend

 - Commuter benefits for team members who report to the SF and NYC office

 - Family planning benefits

 - Matching 401(k) contribution with immediate vesting

 - Flexible PTO policy, plus 80 hours of Sick Time

 - 11 company-paid holidays

 - Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events!

 - Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney

title: Strategic Partnerships & Growth Lead — Civilian Government
description:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the Role

Cursor is the AI code editor used by software engineers across the federal government and the contractors who support them. We are now building a dedicated motion into the civilian Cabinet-level agency ecosystem — DHS, DOJ, DOE, Treasury, HHS, State, and the dozens of bureaus and offices within them that run significant software development operations.

This role owns SpaceXAI's civilian government channel: building relationships with the prime contractors, systems integrators, and federal consulting firms that develop and operate software for Cabinet-level civilian agencies. The mission is to embed Cursor into the software development workflows of every engineer building for the federal civilian government.

Civilian agencies run some of the most complex software in the world — border management at CBP, financial systems at Treasury, scientific computing at DOE national labs, law enforcement infrastructure at FBI. The developers inside those programs need better tools, and Cursor is already being used by individuals inside these agencies. This role builds the formal channel motion to make it the standard.

This is a senior individual contributor role with revenue ownership, reporting directly to sales leadership.


What You'll Do

Prime contractor and channel partnerships

 - Own and grow SpaceXAI's relationships with prime contractors and systems integrators focused on civilian agency programs: Accenture Federal Services, Deloitte Government and Public Services (GPS), Booz Allen Hamilton (Civil division), Leidos Civil, SAIC, CACI, Maximus Federal, Guidehouse, ICF, and contractors supporting MITRE-operated FFRDC programs

 - Negotiate and close partnership agreements — reseller arrangements, teaming agreements, and approved vendor designations — that embed Cursor into software delivery workflows on civilian agency programs

 - Work with prime BD and program management teams to co-sell Cursor into new civilian agency contract awards at the proposal stage

 - Identify and develop relationships with federal consulting firms and boutique civilian-agency integrators that can serve as channel partners or pull-through vehicles

Agency end-user pull-through

 - Build relationships inside DHS (CBP, USCIS, ICE, TSA, CISA, FEMA, Coast Guard), DOJ (FBI, DEA, ATF, USMS), DOE (NNSA, national laboratory network including Sandia, Los Alamos, Lawrence Livermore, PNNL, Argonne, Oak Ridge), and other Cabinet-level agencies at the IT, software engineering, and digital transformation leadership level

 - Engage agency CIOs, CDOs, and digital service offices to build awareness and preference for Cursor within civilian agency software development standards and procurement pipelines

 - Develop relationships with the US Digital Service (USDS), GSA (18F, Login.gov http://Login.gov, cloud.gov http://cloud.gov), and agency-embedded digital transformation teams that influence tooling standards across the civilian government

 - Represent SpaceXAI at ACT-IAC events, AFCEA Federal, agency industry days, and civilian government technology conferences; establish SpaceXAI's presence in the federal civilian IT community

Revenue and pipeline

 - Own a revenue target for civilian government channel business

 - Build and manage a pipeline of prime contractor partnerships and program-level co-sell opportunities across civilian agency programs

 - Forecast and report on channel pipeline with the same rigor as direct enterprise deals

 - Identify and pursue contract vehicles relevant to civilian software tools: GSA IT Schedule 70, CIO-SP4, Alliant 2/3, and agency-specific BPAs and IDIQs

Cross-functional

 - Work with SpaceXAI's legal and compliance teams on teaming agreements, vendor qualification, and FedRAMP authorization planning — civilian agencies are more likely to require FedRAMP than DoD, and this candidate should be able to navigate those conversations honestly and strategically

 - Partner with Field Engineering on technical evaluations and POCs inside prime contractor and agency developer environments

 - Channel civilian agency developer feedback and product requirements back to SpaceXAI's roadmap team — DOE national labs in particular will push requirements for high-performance computing, scientific workflows, and air-gapped environments that no other customer segment will surface
   

What We're Looking For

Required

 - Active Secret clearance — non-negotiable; candidates without an active Secret clearance will not be considered

 - US Citizenship required

 - 5+ years of channel sales, BD, or partnership management experience inside the federal civilian government market, with direct exposure to Cabinet-level agency programs

 - Existing relationships at one or more prime contractors or systems integrators active in the civilian agency market at the BD, program management, or technical leadership level

 - Understanding of civilian government procurement mechanics: GSA Schedule 70, IDIQ vehicles (CIO-SP4, Alliant 2/3), agency-specific BPAs, and the role of FedRAMP in civilian agency software procurement

 - Track record of standing up or expanding channel/partner relationships that drove material software or technology revenue ($500K+) in the civilian federal market

 - Comfortable navigating both the prime-facing channel layer (BD, program managers, contracting) and the end-user pull-through layer (agency software engineers, IT leads, digital transformation offices)

Strong plus

 - Active TS/SCI or DOE Q clearance

 - Prior experience or service at a Cabinet-level civilian agency in a software, IT, data, or digital transformation role

 - Experience selling developer tools, AI/ML platforms, or SDLC tooling through or alongside civilian federal prime contractors

 - Existing relationships at DHS (any component), DOJ (FBI, DEA, or USMS), DOE (NNSA or national laboratory), or Treasury/HHS digital service offices

 - Familiarity with FedRAMP authorization processes and the ability to position a pre-authorization vendor's roadmap credibly in front of civilian agency procurement teams

 - Network within the civilian federal prime ecosystem: Accenture Federal Services, Deloitte GPS, Booz Allen Civil, Leidos Civil, SAIC Civil

 - Understanding of DOE national laboratory culture and procurement — national labs operate outside standard civilian agency procurement in meaningful ways and represent some of the largest software development communities in the federal government

Why this role

Cabinet-level civilian agencies employ tens of thousands of software developers and spend billions on technology contracts annually. Cursor is already being used by engineers inside these agencies and the contractors that support them. The formal channel motion does not yet exist. This role builds it from scratch, with a product developers choose independently, a growing prime contractor presence to build on, and direct access to SpaceXAI's GTM and product leadership.

title: Principal Engineer I, Governance
description:
We’re not just building better tech. We’re rewriting how data moves and what the world can do with it. With Confluent, data doesn’t sit still. Our platform puts information in motion, streaming in near real-time so companies can react faster, build smarter, and deliver experiences as dynamic as the world around them.

It takes a certain kind of person to join this team. Those who ask hard questions, give honest feedback, and show up for each other. No egos, no solo acts. Just smart, curious humans pushing toward something bigger, together.

One Confluent. One Team. One Data Streaming Platform.


ABOUT THE ROLE



Confluent's Data Streaming Platform is only as trustworthy as the schemas, metadata, and policies that govern it. As more of the platform's value shifts toward real-time processing and AI-driven decisioning, the systems that keep data well-formed, reliable, discoverable, and compliant, from the moment it's produced through every downstream consumer, become as critical to correctness as the storage and compute layers themselves. The governance layer and the stream catalog integrates the Data Streaming Platform into a unified, intuitive and intelligent product to serve the critical real-time use cases for our customers.

Confluent Schema Registry - a foundational building block for streaming governance is a widely adopted infrastructure in the industry supporting over 4 Million schemas across 60K customer facing clusters with throughputs as high as 5K reqs/sec for some use cases. Solving complex distributed systems challenges at this scale is one of the core dimensions of this role.

As a Principal Engineer, you will be a key technical leader shaping the long-term architecture, scalability, and reliability of Confluent's schema and metadata governance systems, and their integration across the broader Confluent Streaming Platform. You will focus on advancing the core layers of Stream Governance, including highly available, multi-tenant infrastructure and the systems responsible for schema management, data policy enforcement, and metadata consistency at scale.

You will own company-level technical domains, set direction for critical initiatives, and influence both engineering practices and product strategy. This role requires operating with autonomy in highly ambiguous spaces, making decisions that balance technical depth with business impact to ensure reliability and scalability for governance services across all of Confluent Cloud and Confluent Platform.




WHAT YOU WILL DO



- Technical Strategy & Leadership: Define and drive company-level technical strategy for critical governance systems, ensuring long-term innovation for schema and metadata infrastructure.

- Metadata Architecture & Lifecycle Management: Architect and evolve high-performance metadata management systems that support low-latency lookups, strong consistency guarantees, and coherent behavior across streaming and processing engines.

- Data Policy & Governance Systems: Design and evolve data protection capabilities — including encryption, access control, and schema validation — enforced consistently across the platform.

- Platform Engineering: Build and maintain highly available, multi-tenant infrastructure for governance services, ensuring the platform is optimized for scalability, reliability, and resilience.

- Architectural Excellence: Establish and evangelize engineering standards, architectural patterns, and technical frameworks adopted across the organization.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with executives, product management, and engineering leaders across the platform to align technical vision with business objectives — working across team boundaries to build consensus on shared architecture decisions you don't have direct authority over.

- Mentorship & Culture: Mentor senior and staff-level engineers, growing future technical leaders and shaping a culture of engineering excellence and open-source contribution.

- Open-Source & External Representation: Contribute to relevant open-source projects and represent Confluent externally through technical talks and thought leadership.




WHAT YOU WILL BRING



- Deep Expertise: A proven track record of leading the architecture and delivery of large-scale distributed systems with company-level impact.

- Distributed Systems Mastery: Comprehensive knowledge of fault tolerance, consistency, scalability, and cloud-native platforms.

- Streaming Architecture Fluency: Working depth with streaming or event-driven architectures, and familiarity with adjacent domains such as schema management, data catalogs, or metadata/governance systems.

- Strategic Influence: Ability to navigate ambiguity, reduce systemic complexity, and anticipate industry trends to design systems for the next 3–5 years.

- Leadership Presence: Strong ability to influence executives and stakeholders while fostering a collaborative environment across multiple teams.

- Execution: Demonstrated ability to move from high-level vision to detailed technical implementation and delivery, with a strong bias toward shipped, adopted outcomes over theoretical design.

Vanta is the AI-powered Trust Management platform redefining how businesses earn and prove trust. As a Director of Product, you will lead Vanta’s expansion of agentic workflows, focused on audit and proof outcomes. You will own the strategy and vision for how agentic features and products can accelerate and simplify earning trust through audits, trust centers, questionnaires and more. You will drive an opinionated vision for how LLMs and agentic workflows are natively embedded into enterprise software and own the product strategy and deliver key capabilities that enable Vanta’s GRC product to meet the needs of our largest enterprise customers.



You will drive company-wide initiatives requiring deep partnerships across PMM, engineering, design, and go-to-market teams. You will help scale Vanta’s capabilities alongside our rapidly growing customer base and shape the culture and processes of the product team, all while growing the talented PMs you lead. This role reports directly to the VP of Product for Governance and Compliance.



What you’ll do as a Director of Product at Vanta:

 - Set the vision and product roadmap for autonomous audit agents—transforming manual internal/external audit workflows into automated workflows, powered by AI

 - Own Questionnaire Automation and Trust Centers, turning customer security postures into a competitive growth driver while partnering directly with EPD and GTM leadership to unblock enterprise deals.

   - Enterprise customer adoption and satisfaction metrics.

 - Collaborate cross-functionally to define a vision and roadmap that balances innovation, scalability, and customer impact.

 - 12+ years of Product Management experience with deep enterprise product instincts, having built for complex organization structures and B2B workflows.

 - 5+ years of experience hiring, managing, and growing high-performing teams.

 - A passion for scaling B2B SaaS products that serve SMB and enterprise customers alike.

 - A track record of setting clear product vision and business strategies for complex product areas.

 - Proven experience in a high-growth environment similar to Vanta’s size or larger; if coming from a large enterprise incumbent, must have experience leading a fast-moving business unit.

 - A bias toward shipping and learning quickly

 - A deep commitment to building high-quality products and fostering that culture across the organization.

 - Strong decision-making skills, effectively balancing ambiguity, data, speed, and iteration.

 - Experience with security or compliance products is helpful but not required.



What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

 - Industry-competitive salary and equity

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans

 - 16 weeks fully-paid Parental Leave for all new parents

title: Software Engineer, Data Platform (Foundations Lead)
description:
WHO WE ARE

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.



Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

Notion’s Data Foundations team builds and operates the batch and streaming infrastructure behind our product features, analytics, search, and AI experiences. We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to shape the next generation of this platform as Notion serves larger customers, expands globally, and supports more data-intensive products. You’ll identify the highest-leverage problems, set direction, build and develop a high-performing team, and lead multi-quarter initiatives across our data lake, streaming, distributed-compute, governance, and reliability systems. You’ll stay close to critical technical decisions while creating clear ownership, growing engineers and technical leaders, and helping the team execute as one—partnering closely with Data Engineering, Data Product, Search, AI, Infrastructure, and Security.



This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. 




WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE:

 - Set the direction for Data Foundations. Turn ambiguous company and customer needs into a clear multi-quarter strategy across the data lake, streaming, distributed compute, governance, and platform reliability—and align engineers and partner teams around it.

 - Build and develop a high-performing team. Attract strong engineers, set clear expectations, grow technical leaders, and create an environment of ownership, direct feedback, and accountability.

 - Lead the team’s hardest initiatives from idea to operation. Ensure complex work has strong technical ownership, de-risk architectures through prototypes, break work into shippable milestones, and coordinate execution across engineers and teams.

 - Make Notion’s data platform enterprise-ready. Guide the team toward durable foundations for external key management, data residency, access controls, lifecycle management, and governance without creating separate systems for every requirement.

 - Raise reliability, simplicity, and cost efficiency. Identify systemic risks and architectural gaps, establish clear service ownership, and lead migrations that make Kafka, Debezium, S3/Iceberg, Spark, EMR, Athena, and related systems easier to operate at scale.

 - Multiply the engineering organization. Establish reusable abstractions and paved paths, delegate meaningful ownership, raise the quality of technical decisions, and scale expertise through coaching, documentation, tooling, design reviews, and direct collaboration.




SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: 

 - Deep data-platform expertise. You have designed and operated large-scale batch and streaming systems and can reason across storage, compute, ingestion, orchestration, serving, governance, and production operations.

 - Direction-setting leadership. You have led a Data Platform or infrastructure team through multi-quarter work—finding the right problems, defining a strategy, sequencing execution, and driving decisions with long-term consequences.

 - Team-building and talent development. You have attracted strong engineers, grown people across career stages, developed technical leaders, and created clarity when expectations or performance needed to change.

 - Hands-on engineering judgment. You stay close to critical systems and designs and know when to prototype, simplify, buy, build, or migrate. You can go deep while preserving ownership for the engineers leading the work.

 - Platform-product thinking. You understand the needs behind partner requests and turn repeated patterns into safe, ergonomic, self-serve capabilities rather than accumulating bespoke solutions.

 - Organizational influence. You create clarity across team boundaries, surface uncomfortable technical or organizational risks early, and help engineers do their best work through strong context, delegation, feedback, and coaching.

 - You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, move faster, and build more creatively.




THE SYSTEMS AND PROBLEMS YOU MAY LEAD

 - Evolving Notion’s data lake toward an S3 + Iceberg lakehouse with stronger governance, discoverability, schema evolution, and lifecycle controls

 - Scaling Kafka and Debezium-based streaming infrastructure that powers real-time product, analytics, and AI use cases

 - Improving Spark and distributed-compute performance, workload isolation, developer experience, and cost efficiency

 - Designing EKM, data residency, and compliant processing capabilities across Notion’s data estate

 - Creating clear platform interfaces and self-serve primitives for Data Engineering, Search, AI, and product teams




WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Notion’s data infrastructure is no longer only an internal analytics layer. It increasingly powers customer-facing features, AI systems, enterprise controls, and high-volume product workflows. The team needs a leader who can see across these systems, build the technical leadership and operating culture required for that responsibility, and find the problems that matter before they become roadmap blockers. Success means Data Foundations has a strong, growing team with clear direction and dependable execution—and teams across Notion can build ambitious data-powered products faster without compromising customer trust.



Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. Notion's Search & Context Platform is the substrate that powers how 100M+ users and, increasingly, Notion's agents find and reason over the right information. This team owns the search infrastructure and indexing systems powering lexical and semantic retrieval, the platform primitives for managing agent context and memories, and the scalability, performance, security, and enterprise capabilities that make all of it production-grade.

title: Director of Product Design
description:
At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. 



The Third-Party Risk Management team drives product development excellence across Vanta's EPD organization. This area is responsible for building and improving the tools, practices, and systems that enable product squads to move faster and deliver higher-quality experiences. As Director of Design, you will lead a team of product designers, set the design strategy for the area, and ensure Vanta ships world-class user experiences across your squads.



As a Director of Product Design at Vanta, you will define a net-new experience vision, strategy, and execution for a highly AI-centric workflow builder. You’ll partner cross functionally to align others around your vision and execution, championing your experience strategy to scale your customer impact. You’ll enable Vanta to serve our most complex enterprise use cases while opening up an entirely new class of automation and extensibility across the product.

 
 

What you’ll do as a Director of Design at Vanta:

 - Set the vision and design strategy for Vanta’s Risk product area, helping customers understand, prioritize, and act on risk across their organizations.

 - Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing team of product designers while fostering a culture of craft, experimentation, accountability, and customer obsession.

 - Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Content Design, Design Systems, and Go-to-Market teams to shape strategy and deliver cohesive customer experiences.

 - Translate complex risk management workflows into intuitive, scalable experiences for security, compliance, IT, legal, finance, and business stakeholders.

 - Define experiences that help customers identify, assess, treat, monitor, communicate, and report on risk.

 - Create simple, connected workflows across risks, assets, vendors, controls, tasks, frameworks, owners, approvals, and organizational hierarchies.

 - Guide the design of enterprise-grade risk registers, dashboards, reporting experiences, and workflows that give customers a clear view of their risk posture.

 - Lead customer-centered discovery and research with risk managers, security leaders, compliance professionals, and other Vanta customers to identify meaningful problems and validate solutions.

 - Establish a high bar for interaction design, visual design, information architecture, accessibility, content, and overall product quality.

 - Influence product strategy and roadmap decisions through strong design perspectives, customer insights, prototypes, and compelling narratives.

 - Develop frameworks and processes that help the Risk design team make effective decisions, move quickly, and maintain consistency across complex product experiences.

 - Partner with the Design Systems team to evolve reusable patterns that support a coherent and scalable Vanta experience.

 - Bring clarity to ambiguous, highly complex problems and help cross-functional teams align around a shared vision of the customer experience.

 - Define and measure the impact of design through customer outcomes, product adoption, usability, efficiency, and business results.

 - Help shape AI-powered experiences that make risk management more proactive, actionable, and accessible while applying sound judgment around trust, transparency, and responsible use of AI.

 - Represent Design in leadership discussions, planning processes, product reviews, and other cross-functional forums.

 - Contribute to the broader Design organization by sharing best practices, mentoring leaders and designers, and strengthening how Vanta approaches product design.

 - Working AI-natively: uses AI tools throughout the design process, and has shipped designs for non-deterministic, AI-powered experiences (chat, agentic modalities, etc).



How to be successful in this role:

 - 10+ years of experience designing digital products, including significant experience leading product design for complex B2B SaaS or enterprise software.

 - 4+ years of experience managing and developing product designers, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and career development.

 - Experience setting design direction for a product area and translating company strategy into clear team priorities and outcomes.

 - A track record of designing intuitive workflows for complex, data-rich, or highly configurable products.

 - Strong product thinking and systems thinking, with the ability to understand relationships across interconnected objects, users, workflows, and business processes.

 - Experience partnering closely with Product and Engineering leaders to shape strategy, prioritize investments, and deliver high-quality products.

 - A deep understanding of customer-centered design practices, including qualitative research, journey mapping, prototyping, usability testing, and iterative product development.

 - Strong interaction design, information architecture, visual design, and storytelling skills, with a portfolio demonstrating thoughtful and high-quality work.

 - Experience designing products in risk management, cybersecurity, compliance, GRC, IT, infrastructure, financial services, or another complex and regulated domain is a plus.

 - Familiarity with design systems and experience creating scalable patterns that support consistency across a growing product.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence executives, cross-functional partners, and customers.

 - Comfortable operating in ambiguity, making decisions with incomplete information, and balancing strategic thinking with a bias for action.

 - A collaborative leadership style and a demonstrated ability to build trust, encourage diverse perspectives, and bring teams together around a shared vision.

 - A strong commitment to Vanta’s principles: putting customers first, biasing for action, winning as one team, deciding with frameworks, leading with resilience, and doing what it says on the tin.

 - Required: Bachelor’s degree in Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Computer Science, or a related field.

 - Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.

 - Responsible for protecting Vanta and customer data in how your team operates and delivers results.

 - Open to using AI to amplify your skills and strengthen your work, demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.



What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

 - Industry-competitive salary and equity

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans

 - 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents

 - Health & wellness stipend

 - Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend

 - Commuter benefits for team members who report to the SF and NYC office

 - Family planning benefits

 - Matching 401(k) contribution with immediate vesting

 - Flexible PTO policy, plus 80 hours of Sick Time

title: Staff Product Manager, Data Platform
description:
At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. 



As the Staff Product Manager, Data Platform at Vanta, you will be responsible for product strategy and direction for Vanta’s data platform. You’ll sit between the core platform and feature teams, driving the roadmap for transforming how we fetch, store, and use data from customers and 3rd parties at scale. This platform directly enables customer and business outcomes, and backs Vanta’s products and experiences. This is a highly impactful, technical role at the center of how Vanta works and meets customer needs at real scale. Vanta manages data from over 16,000 customers and is rapidly scaling daily.



You’ll be part of Vanta’s Automation group, which owns how customers discover and connect to other platforms through integrations, use that data to power product experiences and tests, drive customers toward compliance-related security outcomes, and ultimately generate the evidence required for audit. You aren’t building Vanta’s service delivery platform - you’re building the engine that powers compliance and monitoring outcomes. Your team will be Foundations, which has wide scope and depth, and you’ll be the sole PM to support the data platform.



What you’ll do as Staff Product Manager, Data Platform at Vanta:

 - Own the impactful Data Platform roadmap, pairing closely with engineering counterparts to plan durable platform investments that serve our customers and products built on top of customer data

 - Collaborate closely with other product teams to understand what platform investments they need to be successful, get ahead of their roadmaps, and create a plan that balances short and long term needs to support customer outcomes.

 - Directly drive the Vanta data platform strategy and support GRC strategies, creating clarity on sequencing and support as you build the platform and empower teams to use it.

 - Guide the hard tradeoffs between feature development and platform stability, using clarity and empathy to provide clean direction to other teams.

 - Enable and evangelize for the data platform, working with other teams to help encourage platform contribution and usage

 - Work directly with customers to understand unique platform requirements and opportunities including shipping features directly to support an outcome.

 - Look ahead 12-18 months to build a platform that scales with Vanta, including building toward AI native uses and agent operations.

 - Create and measure key metrics and results for platform investments, and own key outcomes around scalability, feature enablement, and queryability.

 - Support an existing team of engineers and tech leads focused on the data platform



How to be successful in this role:

 - Have 6+ years supporting platform teams, with a preference for data platforms or data products. You’ve built and scaled data platforms before, and know how to make platform roadmaps successful.

 - Come having built 0->1 platforms. You’re not just comfortable with mature data platforms, but have experience building new systems over long time horizons with rich communication along the way.

 - Balance independence and strong communication. You don’t need someone to tell you what to build next, are comfortable learning fast and driving priority within your team, and proactively loop in engineering, other PMs, and your stakeholders before decisions land.

 - Have strong frameworks to build complex platforms with clear sequencing, goals, and progress tracking. You know how to tell the unique story of platform work internally and externally.

 - Be intensely curious and collaborative, naturally leaning into pairing with other teams to understand their platform needs, translate them into common requirements, and enable them as they develop new features and products. You’ve earned the trust of other teams and engineers with a track record of clear and unemotional decision making.

 - Be technically sharp with data platform topics. You need to have solid general knowledge of topics like data push/pull, databases and storage, querying, and APIs. You’re able to work seamlessly with engineers on complex topics while translating these clearly to stakeholders.

 - Be outcome oriented, keeping business and customer goals front and center as you build platform, laddering your efforts up to demonstrable impacts.

 - Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.

 - Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.



What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

 - Industry-competitive salary and equity

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans

 - 16 weeks fully-paid Parental Leave for all new parents

 - Health & wellness stipend

 - Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend

 - Commuter benefits for team members who report to the SF and NYC office

 - Family planning benefits

 - Matching 401(k) contribution with immediate vesting

 - Flexible PTO policy, plus 80 hours of Sick Time

 - 11 company-paid holidays

 - Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events!

 - Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney

We set standard base pay ranges for all roles based on function, level, and country location, benchmarked against similar-stage growth companies. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors and may vary based on candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials.

At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply.



About Vanta

We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged. 

Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent.

title: Staff Software Engineer,  Data Governance & Foundations

Staff Software Engineer
description:
We’re not just building better tech. We’re rewriting how data moves and what the world can do with it. With Confluent, data doesn’t sit still. Our platform puts information in motion, streaming in near real-time so companies can react faster, build smarter, and deliver experiences as dynamic as the world around them.

It takes a certain kind of person to join this team. Those who ask hard questions, give honest feedback, and show up for each other. No egos, no solo acts. Just smart, curious humans pushing toward something bigger, together.

One Confluent. One Team. One Data Streaming Platform.


ABOUT THE ROLE:

You'll help build Confluent Cloud's AI capabilities — the layer that lets customers bring AI  and AI agents capabilities directly to their real-time data. Instead of moving data out to a separate system to run inference or build an agent, our customers do it in place, on streaming data, as part of the same platform they already use to move and process events at scale.

As an engineer, you'll own delivery of significant pieces of this product — not just writing code, but deciding how a capability should work across the services that make it up. The interesting problems here rarely live in one place: shipping something like inference-on-streaming-data or an AI agent that reacts to live events touches several systems at once — the user-facing API, the services that manage model and agent lifecycle, the control plane that schedules and runs the work, and the serving layer that actually executes inference. You'll be expected to reason across those boundaries, make sound design calls, and get engineers inside and outside the team aligned on the approach.




WHAT YOU WILL DO:

 - Design and build the backend services (primarily Go, Java, and Python) that run AI and model inference on real-time data.

 - Own features end to end — drafting the design, aligning stakeholders inside and outside the team, and driving the decision to a conclusion.

 - Make the technical calls on systems that span teams: model lifecycle, inference routing, and agent execution.

 - Own the quality of what you ship — code, test coverage, documentation, operability, and rollout safety. This is production infrastructure serving live inference, so reliability isn't an afterthought.

 - Make the engineers around you better through code review, design feedback, and being someone the team trusts with ambiguous, cross-cutting work.

 - Participate in on-call for the services your team owns, and help keep the team's processes and rituals healthy.
   
   


WHAT YOU WILL BRING:

 -  10+ years of significant experience designing, building, and operating distributed systems or cloud-native backend infrastructure in production

 - .Strong working knowledge of Kubernetes and distributed-systems patterns (control loops, API servers, high-scale control planes), plus the fundamentals — containerization, networking, resource isolation.

 - Proficiency in at least one of Go, Java, or Python, and the willingness to work across all three.

 - A track record of leading cross-team technical work: turning ambiguous requirements into designs others can rally behind.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication — you can write a design doc that aligns people who don't report to you.




WHAT GIVES YOU AN EDGE:

 - Exposure to model serving, LLM/agent infrastructure, or streaming data systems.
   
   - You don't need a background in ML research or model training — this role is about building and operating the platform that serves AI reliably at scale, not inventing the models.




READY TO BUILD WHAT'S NEXT? LET’S GET IN MOTION.







COME AS YOU ARE

Belonging isn’t a perk here. It’s the baseline. We work across time zones and backgrounds, knowing the best ideas come from different perspectives. And we make space for everyone to lead, grow, and challenge what’s possible.

title: Director of Ad Sales - West
Staff Product Manager, Cloud Networking
description:
We’re not just building better tech. We’re rewriting how data moves and what the world can do with it. With Confluent, data doesn’t sit still. Our platform puts information in motion, streaming in near real-time so companies can react faster, build smarter, and deliver experiences as dynamic as the world around them.

It takes a certain kind of person to join this team. Those who ask hard questions, give honest feedback, and show up for each other. No egos, no solo acts. Just smart, curious humans pushing toward something bigger, together.

One Confluent. One Team. One Data Streaming Platform.


ABOUT THE ROLE:

Confluent's Cloud Networking team is responsible for making connectivity to and from Confluent Cloud reliable, scalable, secure, cost-efficient, and simple to use — across Kafka, Flink, Connectors, Data Governance, and Tableflow, on AWS, Azure, and GCP.

As Staff PM for Cloud Networking, you will own the platform strategy for how enterprises connect to Confluent Cloud. This is not a feature-level role — you will define the architecture of our networking product surface across all clouds and connection models, set the multi-year roadmap, and operate as a co-decision-maker alongside engineering leadership on the technical direction of the platform. You will work across all networking connection types — PrivateLink, VNet peering, Transit Gateway, Private Service Connect, and egress optimization — and drive alignment across engineering, field, and executive stakeholders on what we build and why.




WHAT YOU WILL DO:

 - Own the platform strategy for Confluent Cloud Networking across AWS, Azure, and GCP — defining the north star, multi-year roadmap, and sequencing of bets that balance customer connectivity needs, cost efficiency, security posture, and engineering leverage

 - Define frameworks and standards that other PMs, designers, and engineers use to evaluate networking decisions — connection model selection criteria, cost attribution models, security control frameworks, and launch readiness standards

 - Drive architectural decisions in partnership with engineering leadership — weighing trade-offs between user experience, cost, and operational complexity

 - Expand scope and create optionality — identify adjacencies the team should move into (network observability, cost transparency tooling, next-generation isolation models) and build the business case for them

 - Develop the product team — mentor Senior PMs on the team, provide feedback on product documents and roadmap thinking, and raise the bar on how the team approaches customer research and decision-making

 - Build senior stakeholder alignment across product, engineering, sales, field, legal, and security, then present the platform vision to executive leadership to secure organizational investment — develop the business case, communicate trade-offs clearly, and earn commitment for multi-year platform bets

 - Define and own success metrics at the platform level — connecting technical milestones to business outcomes including revenue, retention, attach rates, and infrastructure cost efficiency

 - Engage directly with strategic customers and prospects — represent the product roadmap with credibility in technical conversations with enterprise CTOs, architects, and network engineers
   
   


WHAT YOU WILL BRING:

 - 8+ years of product management experience, with at least 3 years owning a cloud infrastructure, platform, or networking product

 - Demonstrated track record of setting product strategy and roadmap at platform or portfolio scope — not just feature-level delivery

 - Deep fluency in cloud networking concepts: PrivateLink, VNet peering, Transit Gateway, Private Service Connect, DNS, security groups, CIDR/IP management, and their trade-offs across AWS, Azure, and GCP

 - Experience owning products that serve enterprise customers with complex compliance, security, and connectivity requirements

 - Proven ability to partner with engineering leadership as a co-decision-maker on architectural direction — not just translating engineering output

 - Strong analytical foundation: can model unit economics, build business cases with cost/risk sensitivity, and measure platform health through leading and lagging indicators

 - Practices AI-native product management — uses AI tools as a genuine thought partner throughout the product lifecycle (research, prioritization, spec writing, analytics), with sound judgment on when to use, override, and validate AI output; and brings that same mindset to product design, building features and APIs that are composable, observable, and easy for AI agents and automation to consume

 - Experience developing PMs and raising the bar on product thinking — through direct mentorship, feedback, or team processes


PREFERRED

 - Experience with Envoy, Service Mesh, DNS and Kubernetes Networking

 - Familiarity with Terraform, API-first and infrastructure-as-code workflows, and how enterprise engineering teams operate networking automation

 - Exposure to network traffic metering, data transfer billing attribution, cost transparency tooling, or pricing and packaging strategy for cloud infrastructure products — defining packaging tiers, price points, and commercial model for enterprise buyers

 - Experience operating in a product-led growth or usage-based pricing environment

 - An MBA degree is a plus
   
   


WHAT GIVES YOU AN EDGE:

 - At the Staff level, we expect more than excellent execution on a defined scope. We're looking for someone who:
   
   - Defines the playing field — identifies problems the team isn't yet working on and builds conviction for why they should be
   
   - Multiplies others — makes the PMs and engineers around them better through frameworks, feedback, and the way they structure problems
   
   - Operates without a ceiling — can go from a whiteboard architecture discussion to a customer negotiation to an executive strategy review, and adds value in all of them
   
   - Takes a position — has a clear point of view on where cloud networking is going and can defend it under scrutiny, while remaining open to updating when given new information

description:

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Today, enterprises stitch together separate systems for streaming, analytics, and serving. Each of these systems come with its own latency, cost, and operational overhead. The next evolution of Confluent's platform collapses that complexity by continuously materializing streaming data into fast, queryable state that serves real-time analytics, operational applications, and downstream intelligent systems from a single foundation.



As a Staff Product Manager, you'll own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the core streaming analytics engine underlying Confluent's real-time data platform. You'll own the engine: the storage, materialization, query layer, and performance, while partnering with peer product managers who own the downstream product experiences built on top of it.



This is a foundational, high-leverage role. You'll define a new product category that brings together concepts from streaming analytics, real-time OLAP, materialized views, and modern database systems into a cloud-native, streaming-first architecture. THE ROLE:

Airbyte is looking for an Engineering Manager, Platform to lead the team responsible for the infrastructure, tooling, and engineering systems that power Airbyte Cloud, Airbyte Flex, and Airbyte Agents.



As an Engineering Manager on the Platform team, you'll lead the engineers responsible for cloud infrastructure, deployment systems, CI/CD, observability, reliability, and the internal tooling that powers engineering velocity across the company.  - Operational toil decreases through automation, not heroics.

 - Experience with data infrastructure, ETL/ELT, or large-scale distributed systems.

 - Experience contributing to open-source engineering organizations.

Platform Engineering is the force multiplier for every engineering team at Airbyte.

title: Principal, User Research
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

At Mural, we believe great collaboration starts with deep understanding. Our mission is to help teams think and work together better. The Design and Research team uncovers the truths that power that mission, guiding product, design, and strategy through rigorous, human-centered inquiry. YOUR MISSION

As the Principal, User Researcher at Mural, you’ll start a UX research practice and lead foundational and strategic research that shapes how the company defines its next generation of experiences. You’ll partner across product, design, sales, marketing, and strategy to identify new opportunity spaces, clarify evolving user needs, and guide the organization toward long-term innovation.

This is a primarily individual-contributor role focused on uncovering deep human collaboration insights that drive strategy, innovation, and long-term vision. You’ll also help shape and scale the UXR discipline at Mural by mentoring designers to confidently run tactical usability studies, and establishing the frameworks and best practices that elevate research across the company. Think of it as being the first research leader at a fast-growing startup, with the reach and resources of a global platform.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Player Responsibilities (Individual Contributor Work):

 - Lead mixed-methods research (qualitative and quantitative) that explores user needs, behaviors, and motivations across multiple product areas.

 - Drive foundational studies that reveal how teams collaborate and what barriers exist in business collaboration, hybrid, and distributed work.

 - Design and execute medium to large-scale studies that combine qualitative depth with quantitative rigor (surveys, logs analysis, segmentation, and concept testing).

 - Develop a tempo where actionable insights are timely and urgently positioned to shape key product decisions.

 - Translate ambiguous questions into clear learning plans and frameworks that guide product and strategy decisions.

 - Build artifacts (archetypes, frameworks, journey maps, mental models) that make complex insights accessible and actionable across the company, leveraging Mural products.

 - Present insights to an executive, cross-functional audience and provide strategic recommendations based on these insights.
   

Coach Responsibilities:

 - Build the research practice: mentor designers, and product partners in research best practices, helping to scale a culture of curiosity and evidence-based decision making.

 - Establish repeatable, high-quality research standards and methodologies across teams.

 - Partner with design and product leadership to shape Mural’s long-term research vision and roadmap.

 - Champion the role of research in early product strategy and company-wide initiatives.
   

Hybrid Responsibilities (Both Player & Coach):

 - Collaborate closely with cross-functional leaders to prioritize research that informs Mural’s most critical next-generation bets.

 - Facilitate workshops and storytelling sessions that bring insights to life and influence direction across product, design, and business strategy.

 - Partner with Data Science and Market Research to integrate behavioral data, attitudinal insights, and business signals into cohesive, actionable narratives.

 - Shape how research connects to strategy, innovation, and experimentation at every level of the company.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 10+ years of UX Research experience, including deep expertise in both qualitative and quantitative methods. PhD optional.

 - Proven track record leading foundational and strategic research that influenced product direction, vision, or long-term investments.

 - Ability to design and execute mixed-methods research independently: from ethnographic and in-depth interviews to survey design and statistical analysis.

 - Scale strategic insights: Experience driving organizational understanding through storytelling, synthesis, and actionable frameworks.

 - Strong systems thinking skills, with an ability to connect human insight to product architecture and long-term design strategy.

 - Experience shaping and scaling research practices in growing organizations.

 - Comfortable working in ambiguity and helping cross-functional teams find clarity and alignment.

 - Strong communicator who can engage both executive and hands-on audiences with empathy, clarity, and conviction.





WHY YOU'LL LOVE MURAL

You’ll shape new ways of working, as we interact with AI, team members, and customers. You’ll work on some of the most compelling and open-ended questions about the future of collaboration: how people align, make decisions, and innovate. title: Senior Backend Engineer, Agent Infrastructure
description:
Airbyte is the data and action layer for AI agents. We give agents fast, accurate, authenticated access to business data across hundreds of sources, so they can discover the entities that matter, reason over real-time context, and take action in the systems they read from, not just observe them.



We started as the open-source standard for data movement and proved the economics of data integration at scale: hundreds of connectors, thousands of companies, and, since 2020, have raised $181M from leading investors including Benchmark, Accel, Altimeter, Coatue, and Y Combinator. As our CEO Michel Tricot puts it, "the last ten years were all about structured data. The future is all about context." We're now building that context infrastructure for production-grade agents on the same open foundation, as agents become the primary consumers of enterprise data.



Our mission is unchanged: make data available and actionable to everyone, everywhere. That everyone now includes AI agents.







THE ROLE:

Airbyte is building the runtime that powers production-grade AI agents.



This is not an ML research or prompt engineering role. We’re looking for an experienced backend or platform engineer who has built complex production systems and has also worked hands-on with AI agents, orchestration, retrieval, or LLM-powered applications.



Our AI Runtime sits between language models and the enterprise systems agents need to understand and act on. It is responsible for assembling the right context, identifying entities across systems, selecting tools and connectors, coordinating execution, validating evidence, enforcing permissions, and handling failures safely.



A user may ask something simple like:

 - “Investigate this customer and tell me what changed.”

Behind that request, the runtime may need to identify the customer across multiple systems, retrieve fresh data, determine which tools to call, coordinate multiple steps, validate the result, and return an answer with evidence the user can trust.



That infrastructure is what you’ll help build.



We’re still early. The architecture is taking shape, but there is significant room to influence how the runtime is designed, how developers interact with it, and how we make agentic systems reliable in production.






WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Build the Runtime

 - Design and implement the orchestration layer that turns natural-language intent into reliable, multi-step execution.

 - Build systems for routing, state management, retries, failure handling, and long-running agent workflows.

 - Develop systems for entity resolution, context assembly, connector orchestration, and evidence retrieval.

 - Build reusable Skills that encapsulate business workflows and domain-specific capabilities.

 - Coordinate connectors, APIs, tools, deterministic logic, retrieval systems, and multiple language models.



Build Reliable AI Infrastructure

 - Design systems that retrieve and assemble the right enterprise context at runtime.

 - Build evidence-backed reasoning with citations and traceability that users can inspect and verify.

 - Implement permission models, freshness validation, and action policies for production environments.

 - Build evaluation, replay, observability, and debugging systems that help us understand why agents succeed or fail.

 - Improve the reliability of systems where model outputs may be probabilistic, but execution cannot be.



Own Products End to End

 - Take ambiguous product ideas from prototype through production.

 - Own features across architecture, implementation, rollout, and iteration.

 - Work directly with Product, Design, Sales Engineering, Customer Success, and customers to understand real-world problems.

 - Write high-leverage code that creates reusable infrastructure for future product areas.

 - Experiment with new agent architectures while maintaining production-grade reliability.




WHAT YOU’LL NEED:

You may be a strong fit if you are fundamentally a backend or platform engineer who has also spent meaningful time building production AI systems.

 - 7+ years of software engineering experience building and operating production systems.

 - Strong backend engineering fundamentals and experience designing distributed systems.

 - Experience building complex systems involving APIs, asynchronous workflows, concurrency, queues, state, retries, or distributed execution.

 - Hands-on experience building production applications using LLMs, agents, RAG, tool calling, MCP, or similar technologies.

 - Experience with orchestration systems, workflow engines, developer platforms, or infrastructure products.

 - Strong system design skills and the ability to reason about reliability, scale, observability, and failure modes.

 - Ability to move quickly from prototype to production without sacrificing engineering quality.

 - Strong product instincts and comfort operating in ambiguous, 0-to-1 environments.

 - Exceptional written communication skills.

 - A strong bias toward ownership and shipping.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building agent infrastructure, agent platforms, or evaluation systems.

 - Familiarity with orchestration technologies such as LangGraph, Temporal, MCP, or similar.

 - Experience with retrieval systems, vector search, search infrastructure, or knowledge graphs.

 - Experience building developer tools or platform infrastructure.

 - Experience with data infrastructure such as Kafka, Iceberg, Postgres, Spark, or modern data warehouses.

 - Experience working on early-stage products where you helped define architecture and technical direction.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Success is not measured by the sophistication of the prompts. It is measured by whether the runtime becomes more reliable, observable, and trustworthy over time.

You’ll build systems that:

 - Assemble the right context and choose the correct connectors, tools, and Skills.

 - Execute multi-step workflows reliably.

 - Recover gracefully when something fails.

 - Produce evidence-backed answers with citations and traceability.

 - Enforce permissions, freshness guarantees, and action policies.

 - Learn from failures through replay, evaluation, and observability.

 - Allow users to focus on outcomes rather than coordinating individual tools themselves.

As the runtime evolves, developers and users should need to think less about the underlying tools and more about what they want to accomplish. The runtime should handle the complexity underneath.






WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

AI agents work impressively in demos. Making them reliable in production is much harder.

The difficult problems are often not the model itself. They are retrieving the right context, connecting to real enterprise systems, maintaining permissions, coordinating multiple actions, recovering from failures, and determining whether an answer can actually be trusted.

Airbyte already connects to hundreds of business systems. We’re building the runtime that allows agents to use that infrastructure intelligently and safely.

If we succeed, developers will not need to rebuild orchestration, retrieval, permissions, evaluation, and enterprise connectivity every time they build a new agent.

title: Staff Systems Software Engineer
description:
Staff Systems Software Engineer

Remote US & Canada



About this role

Most engineering roles at Thatgamecompany ship features to players. This one ships velocity and quality to engineers. Cloud, Gameplay Backend, and Cross-Platform Backend build the services and features the game runs on; you build the systems that prove that work is correct, fast, and ready — before it reaches players. You will build the systems that prove the gameplay feature works — at scale, on every device, on every commit — and the infrastructure that lets a hundred engineers find that out in minutes instead of days. If it runs in production, another team owns it. If it exists to test, measure, or accelerate what those teams build — test harnesses, load/chaos infrastructure, device labs, build/GPU clusters — you own it. Your output is the studio's velocity and the game's quality floor.



On any given day, you might:

Prove correctness and quality before players find the bugs

 - Build and own the studio's functional test automation framework — runner, fixtures, game-state harness, reporting — plus coverage instrumentation that makes untested systems visible

 - Build regression analysis tooling that separates real regressions from noise and attributes them to a commit automatically

 - Improve test suite speed/trust via flake detection, quarantine, parallel sharding, deterministic replay



Find the breaking point on purpose

 - Design load/stress testing systems modeling realistic player behavior, capable of driving launch-scale synthetic traffic against pre-production

 - Build chaos testing capability — fault injection, latency/partition simulation, dependency failure — run safely against real infrastructure

 - Run disaster recovery exercises, measure actual RTO/RPO vs. stated targets, and turn findings into permanent regression tests



Prove quality on real devices

 - Build app quality testing automation — frame time, memory, thermal, battery, cold-start captured automatically and gated in CI

 - Own the device compatibility lab, orchestration, and certification matrix so device support is verified every commit, not the week before ship



Own the infrastructure engineers build on

 - Build/operate on-prem build clusters (distributed compilation, caching, artifacts) and on-prem GPU clusters (scheduling, multi-tenancy, utilization), backing buy-vs-build with real data

 - Design cross-platform developer tools — including AI-assisted tooling (agents, skills, MCP servers) — that reduce toil across Cloud, Backend, and Client Engineering



Make it land

 - Define, instrument, and publish developer velocity/quality metrics (build time, test cycle time, flake rate, escaped defect rate, MTTR) and use them to prioritize your roadmap

 - Drive adoption across teams that don't report to you

 - Mentor engineers in testing strategy, performance analysis, systems thinking

 - Raise the bar through code review, documentation, reducing bus factor



We expect you to

 - Be a passionate gamer who puts players first

 - Treat developer experience as a product — users, adoption curves, a quality bar — not internal plumbing

 - Operate at Staff level: set technical direction studio-wide, influence without authority

 - Be relentless about systems that prevent problems, not just report them

 - Embrace experimentation for ambiguous, complex problems

 - Communicate trade-offs clearly across distributed teams



Required Skills

 - Languages: Python, Golang, C/C++, Jenkins Groovy; Linux shell scripting; fluent English

 - Testing & Quality Systems: Test framework design; load/stress tooling (k6, Locust, Gatling, JMeter); fault injection/chaos engineering; coverage instrumentation; flake detection

 - Performance & Analysis: CPU/GPU/memory/I/O profiling; statistical analysis of noisy benchmarks; regression detection and commit attribution; observability

 - Build & CI at Scale: Jenkins/GitLab CI/CD; Make/CMake; GCC/Clang; distributed build systems/caching; Git/GitLab and Perforce (large-binary workflows)

 - Infrastructure: Linux/macOS administration; bare-metal/on-prem cluster ops; Docker/Podman; Kubernetes; Terraform/OpenTofu; hardware capacity planning

 - Systems Fundamentals: Distributed systems failure modes; TCP/IP and UDP; resilience patterns; disaster recovery planning and execution



Preferred Skills

Mobile device farm operation, Android/iOS build and profiling toolchains, GPU cluster scheduling (Slurm, K8s device plugins, MIG), game engine internals/engine-level test automation, deterministic simulation/replay testing, live service game experience (or SaaS/PaaS/XaaS equivalent), Windows administration, Ansible, TypeScript/Java/Kotlin/Swift, hybrid/multi-cloud management

title: Contract | Senior UI Artist (MARVEL SNAP)
description:
WHO WE ARE

Second Dinner is an independent game development studio that is here to make the most fun games in the world. Not super fun games. Not SUPER DUPER fun games. We mean the MOST fun games. And for our first game, MARVEL SNAP, we’re partnering with Marvel. That’s right, we get to play in the Marvel Universe!!



As a remote-first company, we want the most talented teammates wherever they call home. While our headquarters is in Irvine, California, most of our team is fully remote! We strongly believe a diverse team with varied perspectives makes us a better company, and in turn, will help us make better games. If you can bring something new to the table and expand our point of view, that's a huge upside, and we’d love to meet you!




OUR ART TEAM

At Second Dinner, the Art Team helps define the visual identity of our games and is responsible for creating a cohesive, polished, and memorable player experience.
We believe great game art comes from a combination of strong fundamentals, thoughtful collaboration, rapid iteration, and an obsessive attention to detail. As Game Artisans, we’re constantly creating, refining, experimenting, and raising the bar for what our games can look and feel like.


We work closely with virtually every discipline across the studio, including Design, Engineering, Production, Product, Data, Marketing, and Sound, to create experiences that are both visually compelling and intuitive for players.




YOUR ROLE

As a Senior UI Artist, you will help define and elevate the visual language of MARVEL SNAP across the game's interface and player experience. You’ll own UI art from early exploration through final implementation, translating gameplay and UX requirements into polished, intuitive, and expressive visual experiences. 

You’ll work closely with UX Designers, Game Designers, Engineers, Product, and the Art Director to solve complex problems through clear visual design. This is a hands-on senior role. We’re looking for someone who can independently take ambiguous problems, develop strong visual solutions, communicate their thinking, and drive those solutions through iteration and implementation. You’ll also help establish and maintain UI visual standards, mentor other artists through feedback and collaboration, and contribute to the continued evolution of MARVEL SNAP’s visual identity.



This is a 6-month contract role to start (with possible extension), but if it’s a great mutual fit, it could evolve into a full-time position.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the visual design and execution of UI experiences from concept through final, game-ready implementation.

 - Create high-quality UI assets including screens, panels, buttons, icons, badges, backgrounds, decorative elements, effects, and other 2D graphic assets.

 - Translate UX flows and gameplay requirements into clear, intuitive, and visually compelling UI solutions.

 - Develop visual explorations, high-fidelity comps, prototypes, and style guides that communicate design intent.

 - Collaborate closely with UX Designers, Game Designers, Engineers, Producers, and other artists to solve UI and player-experience challenges.

 - Establish and maintain cohesive visual standards across UI features and systems.

 - Create and refine iconography, typography, layout, color, hierarchy, and other visual-design systems.

 - Design UI interactions and visual states, including transitions, feedback, emphasis, and other moments that make the interface feel responsive and alive.

 - Implement UI art directly in the game engine and work with Engineers to ensure assets are performant, scalable, and production-ready.

 - Rapidly prototype, iterate, and refine designs based on playtesting, feedback, and evolving product requirements.

 - Identify opportunities to improve existing UI and proactively raise the visual quality and usability of the game.

 - Help establish efficient workflows, processes, and best practices for UI art production.

 - Provide thoughtful feedback, and mentorship to other artists when appropriate.
   
   


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - 10+ years of professional UI, UX, or game art experience, with experience contributing to at least one commercially shipped game.

 - A strong portfolio demonstrating exceptional UI design, visual design, iconography, and game interface work. A portfolio is required for consideration.

 - Strong fundamentals in visual design, composition, typography, color, hierarchy, iconography, and information design.

 - Experience taking UI concepts from rough exploration through polished, production-ready assets.

 - A strong understanding of UX principles and human-computer interaction, with the ability to balance usability and visual expression.

 - Experience designing for different screen sizes, resolutions, and aspect ratios.

 - Experience creating visual systems and maintaining consistency across a large number of UI elements and features.

 - Proficiency with industry-standard design tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma, or equivalent.

 - Experience working directly in a game engine and understanding the practical requirements of implementing UI in a game.

 - Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to clearly explain design decisions and incorporate feedback.

 - The ability to work independently, manage priorities, and make sound visual decisions in a fast-moving production environment.

 - A high level of craft and attention to detail, with a genuine passion for making games look and feel great.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE, BUT NOT NECESSARY

 - Experience working on a card game, collectible card game, or strategy game.

 - Experience working on a live-service game with frequent content updates.

 - Experience shipping mobile games or games across multiple platforms.

 - Experience with motion design, UI animation, or interactive prototyping.

 - Experience with Unity or another game engine.

 - Familiarity with UI implementation, scripting, or programming.

 - Experience building or maintaining UI component libraries and design systems.

 - Experience providing mentorship or visual direction to other artists.
